title: Adaptive deployment orchestrator for model-variant routing, shadowing and rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an orchestrator service that runs alongside rollout controller to make deployment-time routing decisions based on model-variant compatibility scores, region capacity tiers, and a dynamic risk budget. Goals: (1) enable fine-grained A/B and canary routing that respects hardware/quantization compatibility; (2) send shadow traffic for telemetry without impacting latency SLOs; (3) provide automated, explainable rollback triggers and staged fallback to lower-cost regional/variant tiers. This ticket covers design and a v1 implementation (control-plane + lightweight runtime hooks) plus integration tests and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Can define a deployment policy that routes X% of live traffic to a canary variant while shadowing Y% to a different variant for telemetry
System computes and surfaces a compatibility score per model variant + region and refuses to route if score < threshold
Automatic rollback triggers fire when canary error-rate or latency regressions exceed configured thresholds for the risk budget window
Tiered fallback completes within configured SLO (target 2s extra latency) and degrades to reserved capacity tier or alternative region when primary capacity is constrained
Integration tests cover a simulated region failure, quantization-incompatible variant, and a noisy-canary scenario with automatic rollback
implementation_notes: Compatibility scoring: combine kernel/runtime compatibility, KV cache layout match, and quantization signature into a 0-100 score; store in model catalog metadata
Routing policy language: add policy stanza to rollout spec with keys {percent, shadow, compatibility_threshold, tier_preference, failover_regions, risk_budget_ms, rollback_conditions}
Lightweight runtime hook: runtime consults orchestrator for a routing decision; fallbacks are applied client-side with cached last-known policy for offline decisions
Telemetry separation: shadow requests must be marked and dropped from billing and SLO aggregation; use dedicated trace tags to avoid metric contamination
Safety: enforce a hard deny if compatibility_score < 50 for any routing that would place traffic on incompatible hardware
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design review): finalize compatibility schema and policy language; get security review (this ticket)
Phase 1 (canary v1): implement orchestrator, implement policy evaluation, wire into canary controller; run internal test cluster canaries (10% traffic)
Phase 2 (shadow + tiered failover): enable shadow telemetry to alternate variants and a failover path to dedicated tier/reserved pool; run 48h soak
Phase 3 (auto-rollback tuning): add regression detectors and risk-budget backoff; validate in canary with synthetic errors and region outage sim
Phase 4 (GA): enable for selected customers behind feature flag and monitor for 2 weeks before full rollout
test_plan: Unit: compatibility score computation and policy parser
Integration: controller + orchestrator + runtime hook with 3 simulated regions and two model variants (quantized vs fp16)
Chaos: kill primary region network plane and assert fallback completes within SLO, assert no data leak from shadow traffic
Performance: measure added decision latency at 50k rps and ensure median decision time < 2ms
E2E: canary that triggers synthetic latency regression should auto-rollback and produce an incident ticket with root cause hints
